messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need a concise integration + gating plan for the FlashAttention adapter (v2/v3) so the kernel-chooser can pick reliably across our workloads. Focus: kernel selection heuristics, batching, KV cache interactions, and an emergency rollback path.

kevin: linking profiling summary I ran this morning — some surprising p95 regressions at seq=1024 with v3 when batch_size small. table below.

kevin: ```
kernel    | seq | batch | p50_ms | p95_ms | notes
----------|-----|-------|--------|--------|--------------------------
flashv2   | 512 | 8     | 8.1    | 12.3   | stable
flashv3   | 512 | 8     | 7.9    | 11.8   | faster
flashv2   |1024 | 1     | 22.4   | 48.2   | OK
flashv3   |1024 | 1     | 24.0   | 62.5   | p95 blowup when kv-hit low
paged-attn |1024| 4     | 30.2   | 72.1   | no prefix-KV cache
```

alisa: re: the kv-hit mention — confirmed: paged-attn and some v3 codepaths bypass our prefix cache which spikes memory and causes tail latency for cold keys.

raj: Important for router: when kv_hit_ratio < 0.8 and seq >= 1024 prefer flashv2 or fallback_attn. Otherwise use v3 for short sequences.

maria: Agree. We should codify simple heuristic in kernel-chooser:
- if seq <= 512 -> prefer flashv3
- if seq in (513..1024) and batch >= 4 -> flashv3
- if seq >= 1024 or batch < 4 -> flashv2 or fallback_attn
- if kv_hit_ratio < 0.6 -> prefer flashv2

maria: Also need a feature-flag strategy. Proposal: staged flag names and scope.

maria: ```json
{
  "ff_attn_adapter": "off | v3_opt_in | v3_adaptive",
  "ff_attn_adapter.v3_adaptive": {
    "percent": 0,\n    "min_batch": 4,
    "seq_threshold": 512
  }
}```

sophia: +1. Start with v3_adaptive at 0% in prod, run 100% in perf-staging for 48h.

kevin: Checklist for staging perf run:
- run perf harness against our 6 canonical prompts (short/med/long, cached/uncached)
- collect events: token.p50_ms, token.p95_ms, gpu_util, kv_hit_ratio, tokens/sec
- enable detailed traces for any request > p95 threshold (configurable)

raj: We should add automatic fallback rules in the config so if p95 increases by >20% over baseline for >15m we flip routed requests to fallback_attn and alert SRE.

infra-bot: note: will create canary host group and telemetry dashboard when engineering creates the feature flag entry.

maria: Emergency rollback CLI (example):
`redwoodctl features set ff_attn_adapter v2_fallback --selector=prod --reason="p95 regression"`

kevin: Also include quick smoke command to reproduce the regression locally:
`python -m perf_runner --model t5-xxl --kernel flashv3 --seq 1024 --batch 1 --runs 200`

alisa: Important: make sure KV warmup step is in the perf harness. We need a warmup phase that hits prefix cache, then measure cold-key behavior separately.

maria: Ops/alerts we want:
- alert if token.p95 > baseline.p95 * 1.2 for > 15m
- alert if kv_hit_ratio drops below 0.6 for > 5m
- alert on GPU memory OOMs or allocation failures (immediate)

ops-bot: added alert templates: "attn_adapter_p95_regression", "attn_adapter_kv_drop", "attn_adapter_oom".

sophia: Security/compliance note — no change needed for private deployments, flags are control-plane only. On-prem customers must opt in manually.

maria: Rollout plan (concise):
1) run full perf suite in perf-staging (48h) with v3_adaptive -> gather traces, regressions, kv stats
2) small prod blast @ 1% for 2h -> check metrics & error budget
3) ramp to 10% over 24h if stable
4) 50% after 48h, then 100% with gradual kernel-chooser weight switch

kevin: Acceptance criteria before each ramp step: p95 change < +10%, tokens/sec >= baseline * 0.98, no new OOMs, kv_hit_ratio trend non-decreasing.

maria: Action items: @kevin run the staging perf and post traces (ETA EOD tomorrow), @alisa add KV-warmup scenarios to harness, @raj add the heuristic into the kernel-chooser config and a kill-switch flag, @sophia coordinate the flag rollout and dashboards.

kevin: noted — I'll upload the perf artifacts to /srv/perf/attn_adapter/2851234567 and ping here when ready.

maria: Thanks. If anyone spots an edge-case (e.g., extremely spiky single-token workloads) call it out here. We'll have a follow-up check-in 36h after staging run starts. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: created dashboard "Attn Adapter — v2/v3 Integration" and linked perf job template.

maria: closing for now — watch the dashboard and we'll resurface if staging shows anything odd.
